title: Train DPO and recover the preferences
goal:
Train a policy over three responses to one prompt, using only preference counts, and check that DPO finds the optimum that Equation 4 predicts.

`C` is a `(K, K)` matrix: `C[i, j]` is how many times response `i` was preferred to response `j`, and `C[i, i] = 0`. The starter gives you `mean_grad(theta, ref_logits, C, beta)`, the gradient of the mean DPO loss over all counted pairs, and `mean_loss`.

Write `train_dpo(ref_logits, C, beta, lr, steps)`. Start from `theta = ref_logits` (the paper initializes $\pi_\theta$ to $\pi_{\text{ref}}$, Section 3), take `steps` plain gradient-descent steps, and return `(theta, losses)`. `losses[t]` is the mean loss before step `t`, so `losses` has `steps` entries. Don't change `ref_logits`: the reference policy stays fixed during training.
hints: Write `theta = ref_logits.copy()`. Without the copy, `theta -= ...` edits the reference in place, and the implicit reward $\beta\log(\pi_\theta/\pi_{\text{ref}})$ is then always 0.
Each step is `theta = theta - lr * mean_grad(theta, ref_logits, C, beta)`. Record `mean_loss(theta, ref_logits, C, beta)` before you update.
When the counts follow the Bradley-Terry probabilities of a true reward $r^*$, the optimum is $\pi^*(y) \propto \pi_{\text{ref}}(y)\exp(r^*(y)/\beta)$. The tests use a learning rate of $8/\beta^2$.
